declarations.docstring: A family of target types indexed by the number of variables.
The distinguished target element associated with an index.
A distinguished generator multiplied by its inverse generator is one.
The target element serving as a right inverse to the indexed generator.
Extracts a complex coefficient at an integral finitely supported exponent.
Multiplication by a monomial shifts the requested exponent and scales the coefficient.
Builds a target element from an integral exponent and a complex coefficient.
The product of two monomials adds their exponents and multiplies their coefficients.
A natural power of a unit-coefficient monomial scales its exponent.
A finite product of unit-coefficient monomials is the monomial at the summed exponent.
The unit-coefficient monomial at the zero exponent is one.
Expresses the value attached to a partition and permutation as a shifted coefficient.
Identifies a shifted target coefficient with a signed multivariate polynomial coefficient.
An auxiliary complex multivariate polynomial for each number of variables.
Rewrites the auxiliary polynomial as a reversal sign times its defining polynomial.
An auxiliary identity used in coefficient extraction.
Coefficient extraction after the polynomial map recovers the original polynomial coefficient.
The additive map casting finitely supported natural exponents to integer exponents.
Casting a finitely supported natural exponent acts pointwise by the natural-number cast.
Pointwise casting of finitely supported natural exponents to integers is injective.
An auxiliary element of the coefficient target for each number of variables.
The unit monomial at the cast auxiliary exponent equals an iterated product of generators.
The cast auxiliary exponent is a sum of singleton vectors weighted by upper-index counts.
Multiplying the auxiliary element by the exponent monomial gives the image of the auxiliary polynomial.
An auxiliary identity concerning the coefficient construction.
A ring homomorphism from complex multivariate polynomials into the coefficient target.
The polynomial map sends each variable to its corresponding distinguished generator.
The polynomial map into the coefficient target is injective.
